claims.text: CQRS gives reading code its own model, separate from the model changes go through (what separates it from CQS); it can run over a single database with two logical models; a separate read database is a more advanced option, not part of the definition.
CQRS does not require event sourcing: event sourcing is an optional addition for the write store (the dotnet guide's simplified CQRS stores current state).

At stage-2 OrderService.CancelOrderAsync calls repository.FindAsync, then order.Cancel(), notifier.Send, repository.SaveChangesAsync(); ShipOrderAsync has the same shape with order.Ship(); PlaceOrderAsync builds `new Order(...)`.
At stage-2 Order.Cancel() throws OrderStatusException for an order whose status is cancelled or shipped; an exception before SaveChangesAsync means nothing is written.

claims.text: EF Core queries returning entity types are tracking by default; FindAsync (no AsNoTracking) returns a tracked Order whose changes SaveChangesAsync detects and writes.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries (Tracking queries)

claims.text: If a query's result set contains no entity types (e.g. Select into the record OrderSummary from scalar columns), EF Core performs no tracking; the SQL selects only the projected columns (orders.id, status, customers.full_name via JOIN).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries, 'Tracking and custom projections'; lesson backend.l2.projection-queries

claims.text: A read side with data of its own (a table only it reads) pays off when a screen needs a shape a query over the write side's tables cannot give cheaply; while a query can, one set of tables for both sides is simpler. Opposing view: a team expecting heavy, differently shaped reads may split early.

Reads need not load the Order aggregate: its rules guard changes, a read changes nothing; loading whole tracked orders with items for a list costs work for values the screen does not show. Context where it is right: a read that must apply a rule only the entity computes.
